key_insight: CoCo-Prover treats theorem proving as a cost-aware orchestration problem, selecting goals symbolically and buying bounded specialist actions only when they improve the proof frontier.
engineering_relevance: This makes large-scale program verification more practical by reducing prover spending while increasing the number of proofs that can be completed across many dependent obligations.
method: Builds a two-level proof graph: an AND/OR proof hypergraph within each declaration plus a lemma-dependency graph across declarations.
Uses symbolic topological selection to decide which open goals to tackle next.
Uses an agentic router to choose among priced specialist prover actions under evolving routing rules.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on five Lean 4 verification benchmarks, where CoCo-Prover achieved the best solve rate on every benchmark, reached up to 100% on two, and cut cost by up to 30.9% versus the strongest baseline.
watch_item: The approach depends on effective routing and bounded specialist invocations, so gains may be sensitive to benchmark structure, prover integration details, and the cost model used in deployment.
paper_title: Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving via Agent Orchestration in Program Verification
